observations.observation: Is the current version (v32) the best-scoring version in the history?
observations.evidence: history.md: v32 scores 0.80731, while v26 reached 0.81897 and v29 reached 0.81830.

observations.observation: Did the leaderboard score drop after per-topic downsampling and SMOTE resampling were introduced?
observations.evidence: history.md: v29 (no SMOTE) 0.81830 -> v31 (downsample + SMOTE + 4500-feature cap) 0.81098 -> v32 0.80731.

observations.observation: Does the current code train LightGBM on a SMOTE-resampled, topic-balanced dataset instead of the real training set?
observations.evidence: current_code.py cells with downsample(), SMOTE(random_state=42).fit_resample and X = balanced_df[feature_select].

observations.observation: Does the current code cap the selected feature list at 4500 features?
observations.evidence: current_code.py: feature_select = feature_select[0:4500], introduced in v30 per history.md.

observations.observation: Were the best-scoring versions (v26-v29) trained without the 4500-feature cap?
observations.evidence: history.md v26 enabled feature_select_wrapper which keeps up to 13000 features; the 0:4500 cap first appears in the v29->v30 change.

observations.observation: Does the task description say the test set resembles the non-Persuade part, whose score distribution differs from the rest of training?
observations.evidence: task.md summary notes: part of train is Persuade with a different score distribution and the test set resembles the non-Persuade part, so forcing a balanced class distribution via SMOTE moves training away from the test distribution.

observations.observation: Does the current code map continuous predictions to scores with plain clip-and-round?
observations.evidence: current_code.py: predictions = np.round(predictions.clip(1, 6)) in the inference cell.

observations.observation: Has OOF-optimised threshold (cut-point) tuning for QWK been tried in any earlier version?
observations.evidence: history.md mentions no threshold optimisation; task.md notes that solutions use per-threshold rounding optimised for QWK.

observations.observation: Is the OOF array that stores fold predictions an integer array that truncates float predictions?
observations.evidence: current_code.py: oof = balanced_df['score'].astype(int).values, then oof[test_index]=predictions_fold (floats) which get truncated.

observations.observation: Does the expert memory recommend restoring the proven configuration when a reproducible regression followed a change and the prior configuration is available?
observations.evidence: memory/attention/t-1-3-choose-a-response-to-an-unsuccessful-searc.md: check E22 (regression followed a change, prior config available) -> Restore the proven configuration, importance 0.72.

observations.observation: Does LightGBM need explicit mean imputation for the feature matrix after removing SMOTE?
observations.evidence: LightGBM handles NaN natively; imputation was only required by SMOTE, which is removed.

action_summary: Restored the training population of the best-scoring versions: removed the per-topic downsampling and SMOTE resampling (introduced in v30-v32, coinciding with the drop from 0.8183 to 0.8073) and the arbitrary 4500-feature cap, so LightGBM with the QWK objective is trained on the full real training set with the complete saved selected-feature list (filtered to columns present). Fixed the OOF array to be float so raw fold predictions are kept instead of truncated. Added OOF-based optimisation of the five ordinal cut-points for QWK (Nelder-Mead from several starts), used at test time only if it beats clip-and-round on OOF by a safe margin; otherwise the original clip-and-round is kept. The rest of the pipeline (DeBERTa and fb3 stacked features, TF-IDF/Count features, 15-fold LightGBM, submission format) is unchanged.
